question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

At gurukul they spend many years together, growing into the best of friends, and ______ was time for each to return to his home, they wept.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. when it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank must join the two ideas — living together as friends and weeping — by showing the time at which the second event happened, so a conjunction of time is required.

◦ "When" is the subordinating conjunction that introduces a time clause, and the impersonal subject "it" is needed with the expression "it was time (for somebody) to do something".

◦ Correct: ... growing into the best of friends, and when it was time for each to return to his home, they wept.

◦ Structure to remember: It is / was time + for + object + to-infinitive — It was time for us to leave.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "instantly it" and Option 2 "soon it" are adverbs, not conjunctions, and cannot introduce the clause here.

• Option 4 "after it" would place the weeping before the departure time and breaks the natural sequence of events described.

NOTE

• Common conjunctions of time: when, while, before, after, as soon as, till, until, since, whenever.

• The word "gurukul" refers to the ancient Indian residential schooling system, where pupils lived at the teacher's home — useful background for comprehension passages.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The television is big, has an excellent picture, and last but not ______ , it's cheap.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. least.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed idiomatic expression is "last but not least", used when mentioning the final item in a list, to make clear that it is no less important than the others.

◦ Correct: The television is big, has an excellent picture, and last but not least, it's cheap.

◦ Here the speaker lists three merits of the television, and the cheap price — mentioned last — is presented as equally important.

◦ "Least" is the superlative of little, so the phrase literally means "last in order but not the smallest in importance".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "close", 2 "final" and 3 "end" all suggest an ending, but none of them completes this set phrase, which cannot be altered.

• Idioms are fixed expressions: changing even one word makes them wrong.

NOTE

• Other useful list-ordering expressions: first of all, to begin with, moreover, furthermore, in addition, finally, last but not least.

• Degrees of little: little – less – least; of much/many: much/many – more – most.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Go down like a lead balloon
option_1: To be received badly by an audience
option_2: Put yourself in a tough position in order to support someone / something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be received badly by an audience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "go down like a lead balloon" means to be received very badly; to fail completely to impress or amuse people. (बुरी तरह नाकाम होना)

◦ Example: His joke about the manager went down like a lead balloon at the office party.

◦ Origin: a balloon made of lead would be far too heavy to float — it would simply drop to the ground, exactly like a speech or joke that falls flat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 describes the idiom to go out on a limb (to take a risk to support someone).

• Option 3 "Surrender peacefully" corresponds to throw in the towel or lay down one's arms.

• Option 4 "To gamble everything you have" is to put all one's eggs in one basket or to go for broke.

NOTE

• Related idioms of failure: fall flat, bomb, come a cropper, go up in smoke, bite the dust.

• The opposite idea — being very well received — is expressed by go down a treat or bring the house down.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

One appointed to act in place of another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Deputy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Deputy" is a person appointed to act in place of, or as an assistant to, another person, especially in that person's absence. (उप / प्रतिनिधि)

◦ The word comes from the French deputer, meaning to appoint.

◦ Examples: Deputy Commissioner, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chief Minister — each acts on behalf of the principal officer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Minister" = a member of the government in charge of a department; the post is not defined by acting in someone's place.

• Option 3 "Officer" = a person holding a position of authority, a very general term.

• Option 4 "Delegate" = a person sent to represent a group at a conference or meeting; the stress is on representation at an event, not on standing in for one individual.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: proxy (a person authorised to act for another, especially in voting), surrogate (a substitute), locum (a temporary stand-in for a doctor or priest), regent (one who rules on behalf of a monarch).

• Word family: depute (verb), deputation (noun), deputy (noun/adjective).

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

It automatically (adjusts) resistance to match the road grade.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. disorganise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adjust" means to alter or set something slightly so that it fits, works better or suits a purpose; to arrange properly. (समायोजित करना)

◦ Its opposite must convey throwing into disorder / upsetting a proper arrangement, and "disorganise" means exactly that — to destroy the order or system of something. (अव्यवस्थित करना)

◦ In the sentence the machine sets the resistance correctly; the opposite would be to disturb that setting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rectify" = to put right or correct — a synonym in spirit, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "order" = to arrange systematically — again close in sense to 'adjust'.

• Option 3 "suit" = to be convenient or acceptable to — related to fitting, so not opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adjust: adapt, modify, regulate, set, fine-tune, accommodate.

• Antonyms of adjust: disorganise, derange, disarrange, upset, disturb.

• The prefix dis- reverses meaning: disorganise, disagree, disconnect, dishonest, disobey.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

After recess, the students returns to their desks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. returned to their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two points decide this question — subject–verb agreement and the correct spelling of the possessive.

◦ The subject "the students" is plural, so the singular verb "returns" is wrong; the narrative describes a completed past event, so the simple past "returned" is correct.

◦ "Their" is the possessive adjective (belonging to them) and is right before the noun desks; "there" refers to a place and would be meaningless here.

◦ Corrected sentence: After recess, the students returned to their desks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "returned to there" fixes the verb but uses the wrong homophone.

• Option 2 "return to there" is wrong in both respects.

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong because the printed "returns" does not agree with the plural subject.

NOTE

• Homophone trio: their (possessive — their books), there (place — sit there), they're (they are).

• Note also the collocation "return to" a place: return to school, return to their desks — but return home takes no preposition.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Allergies can indirect cause you to feel tired by robbing you of sleep.
option_4: cause you to feel tired by
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Allergies can indirect

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the use of the adjective "indirect" where an adverb is required.

◦ The word modifies the verb "cause" — it tells us how allergies cause tiredness — and verbs are modified by adverbs.

◦ The correct adverb is "indirectly".

◦ Corrected sentence: Allergies can indirectly cause you to feel tired by robbing you of sleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "cause you to feel tired by" is correct — the structure "cause somebody to do something" takes the to-infinitive.

• Segment "robbing you of sleep." is correct — the preposition "by" is properly followed by the -ing form, and "rob somebody of something" is the standard collocation.

NOTE

• Remember: rob a person of a thing but steal a thing from a person — They robbed him of his watch / They stole his watch.

• Adjective → adverb: direct → directly, indirect → indirectly, quick → quickly, easy → easily.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

Bonaparte, unlike Hoche, was not (eagerly to embark in) a serious Irish expedition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. eager to embark on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed segment contains two errors, and only Option 1 corrects both.

◦ After the linking verb "was not", an adjective is needed, not the adverb 'eagerly' — so "eager" is correct.

◦ The verb "embark" takes the preposition "on/upon" when it means to begin an important or difficult task: embark on a project / an expedition.

◦ Corrected sentence: Bonaparte, unlike Hoche, was not eager to embark on a serious Irish expedition.

◦ "Eager to + base verb" is the standard structure: eager to learn, eager to help.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because of the adverb and preposition errors.

• Option 3 "eagerest to embarked on" is doubly wrong — the superlative of eager is most eager (never 'eagerest'), and 'embarked' cannot follow 'to'.

• Option 4 "eager into embark in" uses two wrong prepositions and no infinitive marker.

NOTE

• Note the two senses of embark: embark on a ship (to board) and embark on/upon a venture (to begin).

• Adjectives of two or more syllables form the comparative and superlative with more / most: more eager, most eager.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

You will ______ the price for this crime.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "pay the price (for something)", which means to suffer the unpleasant consequences of one's actions. (कीमत चुकाना / भुगतना)

◦ Correct: You will pay the price for this crime.

◦ Example: He ignored every warning and is now paying the price for it.

◦ The related expression "pay the penalty" carries the same sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "make" does not collocate with 'the price'; one sets or fixes a price.

• Option 3 "pale" means to become pale in colour (a verb) or light in colour (an adjective).

• Option 4 "call" does not fit; "call the price" is not English in this sense.

NOTE

• Other collocations with pay: pay attention to, pay a visit, pay heed, pay respects, pay a compliment, pay off (to be worthwhile).

• Do not confuse pay the price (suffer consequences) with at any price (whatever the cost) and cheap at the price (worth the money).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The frequency of large wildfires ______ dramatically in recent decades.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has increased.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The frequency" — a singular noun. The words "of large wildfires" form a prepositional phrase and do not change the number of the subject.

◦ A singular subject takes "has", so the correct present-perfect form is "has increased".

◦ The time expression "in recent decades" describes a period stretching from the past up to now, which is exactly when the present perfect is used.

◦ Correct: The frequency of large wildfires has increased dramatically in recent decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "have increased" wrongly agrees with the nearby plural noun wildfires instead of the real subject — the classic trap in such questions.

• Option 3 "increase" is the plural present form and does not agree with the singular subject.

• Option 1 "did increase" is an emphatic simple past and does not suit the ongoing period "in recent decades".

NOTE

• Golden rule: the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, never with a noun inside an intervening phrase — The box of chocolates was empty.

• Present-perfect signal words: since, for, so far, recently, in recent years/decades, already, yet, just.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Victorious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Champion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Victorious" means having won a victory; triumphant. (विजयी)

◦ "Champion" refers to a winner — one who has defeated all rivals in a competition — and is therefore the closest in meaning among the options.

◦ Example: The victorious team returned home as national champions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Unsuccessful", Option 3 "Failing" and Option 4 "Losing" are all antonyms of victorious — the examiner has filled the paper with opposites to test careful reading.

NOTE

• Synonyms of victorious: triumphant, winning, conquering, successful, champion.

• Antonyms of victorious: defeated, beaten, vanquished, unsuccessful, losing.

• Word family: victory (noun), victor (the winner), victorious (adjective), victoriously (adverb).

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

I'm sorry I snapped at you earlier, I think I (am just in a bad mood today).
option_4: got up on the wrong side of the bed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. got up on the wrong side of the bed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get up on the wrong side of the bed" means to be in a bad mood or irritable for the whole day for no clear reason. (सुबह से मूड ख़राब होना)

◦ The bracketed part "am just in a bad mood today" carries exactly this sense, and the speaker's apology for snapping confirms it.

◦ Correct: I'm sorry I snapped at you earlier, I think I got up on the wrong side of the bed.

◦ Origin: an old superstition held that leaving the bed on the left side would bring bad luck for the day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "two wrongs don't make right" is a proverb meaning that a second wrong act does not correct the first.

• Option 2 "clam up" means to become silent and refuse to speak.

• Option 3 "dressed to the nines" means dressed very smartly and elegantly.

NOTE

• Other mood idioms: have a chip on one's shoulder (be resentful), fly off the handle (lose one's temper suddenly), in high spirits (cheerful), down in the dumps (depressed).

• "Snap at somebody" in the sentence means to speak sharply and angrily.

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. KNOWLEDGE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Knowledge" is correctly spelt — k-n-o-w-l-e-d-g-e, with a silent k at the beginning and -edge at the end.

◦ It means facts, information and skills acquired through experience or education. (ज्ञान)

◦ Word family: know (verb), knowledge (noun), knowledgeable (adjective).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "LIHGTNING" is wrong; the correct spelling is "LIGHTNING" (the flash in the sky) — note that lightening with an 'e' means making lighter.

• Option 3 "OCCASSION" is wrong; the correct spelling is "OCCASION" — double c, single s.

• Option 4 "MILLENIUM" is wrong; the correct spelling is "MILLENNIUM" — double l and double n (from Latin mille = thousand + annus = year).

NOTE

• Words with a silent k: know, knee, knife, knock, knot, knight, knuckle.

• Other double-letter traps: accommodation, embarrass, committee, possession, necessary, occurrence, harass.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I'll see you in the meets next week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. at the meeting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed, and only Option 1 makes both.

◦ The correct noun is "meeting" — an organised gathering of people. "Meets" is used mainly for sporting events (a swimming meet) and does not fit the sense here.

◦ The correct preposition for being present at an event is "at": at the meeting, at the party, at the conference.

◦ Corrected sentence: I'll see you at the meeting next week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "in the meets" is unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "of the meeting" shows possession and cannot express place.

• Option 4 "on the meeting" would mean about the meeting (as in a report on the meeting), not the place where the people will meet.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place with events: at a meeting/party/wedding; in a room/building/city; on a street/floor/page.

• Related collocations: hold / attend / chair / call / postpone a meeting.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Able to do many different things
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Versatile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Versatile" means able to do many different things well; adaptable and having many uses. (बहुमुखी प्रतिभा वाला)

◦ Example: He is a versatile artist who sings, paints and acts equally well.

◦ It comes from the Latin versare = to turn — hence one who can turn easily from one task to another.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Monastery" = a building where monks live.

• Option 3 "Omnipotent" = all-powerful; having unlimited power (prefix omni- = all) — power, not variety of skills.

• Option 4 "Niche" = a small specialised segment of a market, or a recess in a wall.

NOTE

• Related omni- words: omnipresent (present everywhere), omniscient (knowing everything), omnivorous (eating both plants and flesh).

• A close phrase is the idiom "jack of all trades" — one who can do many kinds of work, though it often carries the tail "but master of none".

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Anomaly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Regularity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Anomaly" is something that deviates from the normal or expected pattern; an irregularity. (विसंगति / असंगति)

◦ Its direct antonym is "Regularity" — the state of being normal, usual and following a fixed pattern. (नियमितता)

◦ Example: The scientists could not explain the anomaly in the readings, which otherwise showed perfect regularity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Omen" = a sign of something that is going to happen in the future.

• Option 2 "Tangible" = able to be touched; clear and definite.

• Option 4 "Tangent" = a straight line touching a curve at one point; the idiom go off on a tangent means to change subject suddenly.

NOTE

• Synonyms of anomaly: irregularity, aberration, deviation, oddity, abnormality, exception.

• Antonyms of anomaly: regularity, normality, conformity, uniformity, consistency.

• Word family: anomalous (adjective), anomaly (noun).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Both men and women consider a variety of concerns when selecting there outfits.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. when selecting there outfits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the word "there", which must be replaced by the possessive adjective "their".

◦ The sentence speaks of the outfits belonging to the men and women, so the possessive form is required: "their outfits".

◦ "There" is an adverb of place (Sit there) or an introductory word (There is a book), and it can never come before a noun to show possession.

◦ Corrected sentence: Both men and women consider a variety of concerns when selecting their outfits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment "Both men and women" is correct — "both ... and" is the proper correlative pair and makes the subject plural.

• Segment "consider a variety of concerns" is correct — the plural verb consider agrees with the plural subject.

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because of the homophone mistake.

NOTE

• The trio their / there / they're is one of the most frequently tested spelling traps in SSC exams.

• With "both ... and", the verb is always plural: Both he and she are coming.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: You will be here for seventy-two hours.
option_2: You will be heare for seventy-two hours.
option_3: You will be here for sventy-two hours.
option_4: You will be here for seventy-two huors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. You will be here for seventy-two hours.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Option 1 every word is spelt correctly — "here", "seventy-two" and "hours".

◦ Here = h-e-r-e, meaning in this place.

◦ Seventy = s-e-v-e-n-t-y; compound numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine are written with a hyphen — seventy-two, thirty-five, ninety-nine.

◦ Hours = h-o-u-r-s, with a silent h in pronunciation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — "heare" is wrong; the correct spelling is "here" (do not confuse it with hear, meaning to perceive sound).

• Option 3 — "sventy-two" is wrong; the correct spelling is "seventy-two".

• Option 4 — "huors" is wrong; the correct spelling is "hours".

NOTE

• Homophones to remember: here / hear, hour / our, their / there, peace / piece.

• Words with a silent h: hour, honest, honour, heir, ghost, rhyme — note that these take an as the article: an hour, an honest man.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

It'd be really cool if you got / on the team, I've never seen you / played badminton, are you good?
option_2: on the team, I've never seen you
option_4: It'd be really cool if you got
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. played badminton, are you good?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the verb form after the verb of perception "seen".

◦ Rule: verbs of perception — see, hear, watch, notice, feel — are followed by the bare infinitive (V1) or the -ing form, never by the past form.

◦ So "I've never seen you played badminton" must become "I've never seen you play badminton" (the whole action) or "...seen you playing badminton" (the action in progress).

◦ Corrected sentence: It'd be really cool if you got on the team, I've never seen you play badminton, are you good?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "It'd be really cool if you got" is acceptable — the contraction It'd (It would) with the past form in the if-clause forms a normal Type 2 conditional.

• Segment "on the team, I've never seen you" is correct — American usage says on the team, and the present perfect with never is right.

NOTE

• Compare: I saw him cross the road (I saw the complete action) and I saw him crossing the road (I saw it in progress).

• In the passive, however, these verbs take the to-infinitive: He was seen to cross the road.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Feat
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Accomplishment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Feat" is an achievement that requires great courage, skill or strength. (उपलब्धि / कारनामा)

◦ "Accomplishment" means something difficult that has been achieved successfully, and is therefore the closest synonym.

◦ Example: Climbing Everest without oxygen is a remarkable feat (accomplishment).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hallowed" = holy, sacred, greatly revered.

• Option 2 "Handsy" is an informal adjective meaning inclined to touch others inappropriately.

• Option 4 "Obligation" = a duty or something one is bound to do, which is a responsibility, not an achievement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of feat: achievement, accomplishment, exploit, attainment, triumph, deed.

• Do not confuse the homophones feat (an achievement) and feet (the plural of foot).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. takes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states a general fact about planking, so the simple present tense is required.

◦ The subject "Planking" is a singular gerund, so the verb must carry -s: "takes".

◦ The first verb in the sentence, "is" (Planking is free), is also present tense, so "takes" keeps the tense consistent.

◦ The collocation is "take + time": It takes only a couple of minutes.

◦ Correct: Planking is free and takes only a couple of minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "taken" is a past participle and cannot stand alone as a finite verb.

• Option 2 "has taken" is present perfect, which would wrongly suggest a completed action rather than a permanent fact.

• Option 4 "took" is simple past and clashes with the present-tense "is".

NOTE

• The simple present is used for universal truths, habits and permanent situations: Water boils at 100°C.

• Verb forms: take – took – taken.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause is elliptical — "no gym membership or special equipment (is) required" — meaning none is needed.

◦ This supports the writer's point that planking is free and convenient: it costs nothing and needs no apparatus.

◦ "Required" means needed or necessary, and it is the standard word used with equipment and qualifications.

◦ Correct: ... no gym membership or special equipment required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "registered" = officially recorded, which does not fit 'equipment'.

• Option 3 "catered" = provided food or services for, used with the preposition for/to.

• Option 4 "placed" = put in a position, meaningless here.

NOTE

• "No ... required" is a common elliptical construction in notices and advertisements: No experience required, No booking required.

• Word family: require (verb), requirement (noun), requisite (adjective/noun).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. core.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In fitness, the "core" means the group of muscles around the trunk — the abdomen, back and pelvis — that stabilise the body.

◦ The passage says heavy movements such as squatting and dead-lifting are hard to do safely "without a strong ______", and the very next sentence confirms it: "Planking provides you with better core strength".

◦ Correct: ... is hard to do without a strong core.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "spot", Option 3 "space" and Option 4 "matter" have no connection with muscular strength and do not collocate with 'strong' in this sense.

NOTE

• Cloze technique: when the same idea is repeated later in the passage ("core strength"), that repetition is the strongest clue to the missing word.

• "Core" also means the central or most important part of something: the core of the problem, core subjects, the earth's core.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. exercises.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "these" refers back to the activities just listed — squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead — and all of them are exercises.

◦ Correct: "We need to keep our spine straight to do these exercises."

◦ The whole passage is about physical fitness, so 'exercises' is the natural noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "therapies" = treatments for an illness, not fitness movements.

• Option 3 "surgeries" = medical operations.

• Option 4 "mechanics" = the study of motion and forces, or the workings of something.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, a demonstrative such as these / those / such always points back to something already mentioned — locate that reference first.

• Fitness vocabulary worth knowing: squat, dead-lift, plank, brace, posture, stamina, flexibility.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. movements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expert is speaking about bracing the body while performing the exercises, and the general word for such physical actions is "movements".

◦ Correct: "Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these movements."

◦ Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead are all movements of the body under load, so the word fits both the sense and the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "drives" would mean journeys by car or organised campaigns.

• Option 2 "competitions" and Option 4 "games" both refer to contests, whereas the passage is about individual exercise, not sport against others.

NOTE

• "Brace" here means to tighten the muscles in preparation for effort or impact.

• Note the useful preposition: "during + noun" (during these movements) versus "while + -ing" (while performing these movements).
